title: indigo_mount_lx200: a position readback failure during motion can end a successful GoTo in ALERT; abort may lose a kept ALERT while decelerating
description: (1) meade_read_position() failing once while the mount is slewing publishes ALERT after BUSY, which is then kept, so a GoTo that completes correctly ends as ALERT. (2) On real hardware an abort publishes BUSY while the mount decelerates, which clears a kept ALERT of the refused request; the simulator stops at once and does not show this. Part 2 needs hardware or a simulator with deceleration. Found while working on ticket 42b85be0-1f19-4607-b3c3-746e60317d17 (closed, commit a09e0f878), which introduced the kept coordinates ALERT in indigo_update_coordinates(): an ALERT published after a BUSY stays until the next BUSY. Reproduce in the driver's simulator suite before changing code.

outcome.summary:
Independent review of master...HEAD (ee9e11a26). No blocking findings.

Verified: (1) meade_update_mount_state() (indigo_mount_lx200.driver:3683-3771): position_failures reset on every successful readback (3692, aGotino 2775) and at connect in meade_init_mount (3545-3547); a failed readback while coordinates are BUSY and position_failures <= POSITION_READ_RETRIES (2) keeps BUSY with the last values and targets untouched, third consecutive failure or a failure while not BUSY is ALERT; aGotino second readback counts once per poll (2769-2779). Same scheme as nexstar 82a1098a1. All coordinates states still published only through indigo_update_coordinates(); kept-ALERT semantics of indigo_mount_driver.c update_coordinates() (1389-1399) hold: a third-failure ALERT after BUSY is kept, recovery OK is published as ALERT until the next request. (2) stopping: set only in the successful-abort branch (4743), cleared on successful goto (4702), park (4588), home (4658), manual motion start (4796, 4814), on any poll that reaches the not-slewing branch (3768) and at connect (3545). Paths that start a slew all pass through one of these (agent uses MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES; ZWO/Gemini/AP/ToupTek park and home stages start inside meade_park/meade_home); sync, tracking and guiding do not start slews; abort failure does not set it; generic/classic/stargo2 inference sees no position change once the axes stand and clears it. (3) Simulator v6: stop_ramp default false, creep/halt/arrive only via control file, single-rule control files behave as before; the new 'fault <cmd>' event lines do not match exact or prefix counters in test_mount_lx200_simulator.c or test_mount_asi_simulator.c. (4) Regenerated .c/.h/_main.c with the worktree indigo_generator from the .driver in scratch: byte-identical. Version 86->87, simulator 5->6, MIGRATION_STATUS 168->171 (165+3 tcp -> 168+3), Comment column untouched; README change is only the run record; no generator/library/mount_asi/PROPERTIES change; form

Implementer record (driver version 86 -> 87, simulator version 5 -> 6).
Part 1 root cause: meade_update_mount_state() set MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES ALERT on every failed meade_read_position() (driver line ~3678 before the change), and the aGotino re-read in meade_update_agotino_state() did the same; an ALERT after the BUSY of a goto is kept by indigo_update_coordinates(), so a goto completing in the poll of a failed readback ended ALERT. Fix (as mount_nexstar 82a1098a1 / mount_ioptron 333445a20): position_failures counter, POSITION_READ_RETRIES 2; a failed readback while the coordinates are BUSY keeps BUSY (slew light BUSY) and the next poll retries; the third consecutive failure, or a failure while not BUSY, is ALERT. Shared by all dialects; the aGotino second readback counts once per poll.
Part 2: reproducible after a simulator extension. Sequence: abort publishes 'Goto aborted' ALERT (kept); the mount decelerates and its controller still reports the slew; the next poll's slewing branch publishes BUSY, which clears the kept ALERT, and the aborted goto ends OK short of its target. Simulator: --stop-ramp lets the axes coast on after :Q#, still slewing, until the 'halt' control (deceleration of a real mount, length decided by the test). Fix: PRIVATE_DATA->stopping set by a successful abort, cleared by a goto/park/home/manual start or by a poll that sees the axes stand; while set, a reported slew lights the slew light but leaves the coordinates state alone.
Simulator test controls added: fault-rule queue (up to 4 lines, fired in order), optional 'arrive' action (the slew ends at its target when the rule fires), 'creep' control (current or next slew at 1/100 speed), 'halt', fired rules logged as 'fault <cmd>' in the event log.
Reproduction on the unchanged driver: lx200_goto_survives_failed_position_readback failed in all 16 dialects (goto ended ALERT); lx200_goto_ends_alert_when_position_readback_keeps_failing failed (ALERT after 1 failure, not 3); lx200_goto_abort

Version 86->87, simulator 5->6, MIGRATION_STATUS 168->171 (165+3 tcp -> 168+3), Comment column untouched; README change is only the run record; no generator/library/mount_asi/PROPERTIES change; formatting per AGENTS.md.

Tests run in a scratch copy under the lock (mac arm64): lx200_goto_survives_failed_position_readback, lx200_goto_ends_alert_when_position_readback_keeps_failing, lx200_goto_abort_keeps_alert_while_decelerating, lx200_classic_timed_guiding, lx200_goto_abort_ends_alert_and_idle_abort_keeps_state: all pass. Mutation check with master's indigo_mount_lx200.c: the three new cases fail (16/16 dialects end ALERT; persistent case fails; 12/12 status dialects publish 3 BUSY during the coast). New cases are event-driven (control rules plus poll-count waits, bounded timeouts). Adjusted classic case still proves the guard at 3732: without it the first failed poll would clear classicGoto (no position change -> not slewing) and the guider would be admitted.

Non-blocking: (a) an abort while nothing moves sets stopping until the next poll (<=1 s); a slew started from a hand controller in that window or during a deceleration would run with the slew light BUSY but coordinates not BUSY. Setting stopping only when something was moving would close it; negligible in practice. (b) position_failures is not reset when a new goto starts, so a goto issued right after a failed poll tolerates one fewer retry; same as the nexstar fix. (c) Part 2 is not covered for generic/classic/stargo2/aGotino or for deceleration after a manual-motion abort; documented in the ticket note. Hardware not run.

Side effect to note: the first scratch build used the copied Makefile.inc whose INDIGO_ROOT points at the worktree, so make relinked the worktree's gitignored build/lib/libindigo.dylib from identical sources; git status of the worktree is clean.

After the fix all three pass.
Test adjusted: lx200_classic_timed_guiding expected one failed :GR# during a goto to publish ALERT (the defect); it now injects three failures on a creeping goto, keeping its intent (a readback failure during a classic goto keeps the guider refused).
